title: Technology Sector Update for 11/19/2018: TSM,ZAYO,AAPL,SOL,BX,KKR,IBM,INTC
text:

Steep declines for technology stocks Monday again weighed on the broader U.S. markets, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 Monday were losing nearly 3.9% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was dropping more than 3.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) just over 2% lower late Monday afternoon, staying with relatively close range of its session low, amid reports the specialty chipmaker is expected to soon land an order for server chips from IBM ( IBM ). The Nikkei Asian Review, citing unidentified supply chain sources, said the chips will be placed in IBM's next-generation mainframe servers, which is trying to challenge industry leader Intel ( INTC ) in the data center sector.
In other sector news:
(+) Zayo Group Holdings ( ZAYO ) was almost 9% higher this afternoon, drifting off a 20% spike soon after Monday's opening bell that followed reports the bandwidth infrastructure company has attracted buyout interest from several prominent private-equity firms, including Blackstone ( BX ) and KKR (KKR) and Stonepeak Partners since Nov. 7 detailing plans to split into two publicly traded companies. Funds managed by I Squared, GTCR and Charlesbank also have expressed interest in a going-private transaction, Bloomberg News said, citing sources familiar with the matter.
(-) Apple (AAPL) was sliding almost 4% lower following reports the technology giant has trimmed production orders for its three recently released iPhone models amid slower-than-expected demand. According to the Wall Street Journal, Apple has cut its production order for the iPhone XR by up to a third from its initial projections expecting to sell nearly 70 million handsets.
(-) ReneSola (SOL) declined Monday after the solar-energy reported Q3 net income and revenue below the comparable quarter last year . The company earned $0.01 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, down from $0.02 per share during the prior-year period although the company still managed to match the single-analyst call. Revenue dropped to $18.8 million from $36.3 million last year, narrowly trailing the single analyst call looking for $19 million.
